issue_context.title: `gh auth setup-git` requires a login
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

`gh auth setup-git` should be used to configure the github credential helper (basically `git config --global credential.https://github.com.helper !'$PATH_TO_GH.EXE' auth git-credential`  however the command fails with `You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate.`

as the command is purely configuring git there should be no requirement for it to be logged in.  this causes pain where the command is being run to pre-setup developer environments but leaves the login to the user at a later date (when it is needed)

```
gh version 2.40.1 (2023-12-13)
https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.40.1
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. on a clean machine download and install but do not configure `git` and `gh`
2. `gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com`
3. `git config --global -l`


### Expected vs actual behavior

the command in step 2 runs without error
the command in step 3 shows that the helper has been added

Actual behaviour is the second command fails

```shell
> gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com
You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate.
```
### Logs
comments: @jtnord Thanks for writing in. I think you make a good point in that allowing `auth setup-git` to be run before authenticating is useful for doing pre-setup of developer environments. It should be simple enough to add the `skipAuthCheck` annotation to the `auth setup-git` command, going to open this up for contributions.

@williammartin Thanks for the correction, 🤦, I did not actually look at the code and just assumed it was using the same `skipAuthCheck` mechanism other commands are using.

I concur that the auth check should only be skipped if the `hostname` flag is provided.

@jtnord @samcoe on reviewing this a bit more, I wonder whether it might be better to provide a `--force` flag in combination with `--hostname"?

There's still some advantage to the current behaviour where running `setup-git --hostname github.con` provides a useful error. In the case where you really, really want to add a credential helper for an unknown host, then you can opt in to `--force`. WDYT?
@williammartin I think that is a good suggestion. I am on board with that approach 👍

This has been merged into `trunk` if you'd like to try it. Our release cadence is roughly every two weeks and we released yesterday. It may go out next week at the earliest. Thanks everyone for your contributions!

review_comments:
I was getting below error for the test cases to check flag.
**panic: unable to redefine 'h' shorthand in "setup-git" flagset: it's already used for "hostname" flag [recovered]**

I observed most of the test cases in gh cli used below code to get rid of this error. 
`cmd.Flags().BoolP("help", "x", false, "")`

So used it for setup-git's test-cases.
Yeh it's super janky. The issue is that `-h` is used for hostname but it's configured outside each individual command, so in the tests we update help to have shorthand of `-x`. 🤮
We're testing the return from a function, so I'd rather use the real type rather than the string form of that type like we might test in the stdout.
Changed these to use `require` which I'm quite opinionated about.
Please ensure you have `expectedHostsSetup` as well since this test currently only asserts that there is no error.
Doesn't look like this was resolved.

I noticed in the existing code that `--hostname` without `--force` would return with different errors depending on whether there were known hosts or not, and that seemed like a bad UX.

To sort this out, it made more sense to just branch early based on whether a hostname had been provided or not. This also has a symmetry with the flags because we can ignore `--force` entirely after the `--hostname` block.
